Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 99, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake (1) And the earth brings forth its burdens (2) And man says, "What is wrong with it?" (3) That Day it will report its news (4) Because your Lord has inspired it (5) That Day the people will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds (6) So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it (8)﴾.

His saying, dhikruhu [exalted is He], means: ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ for the establishment of the Hour ﴿with its (final) earthquake﴾, meaning it is violently convulsed. The word zilzal (earthquake) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) when the zay is kasra, and when the zay is fatha it is a noun. The earthquake is attributed to the earth, though it is its attribute, as one says, "I will honour you with your honour," meaning, "I will honour you with honour." This was made good in the phrase zilzaluha because it matches the rhyme endings of the verses that follow.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: "﴿The earth was shaken﴾ in the time of ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud). ʿAbdullah said to it, 'What is the matter with you? Indeed, if it had spoken, the Hour would have been established.'"

* *

His saying: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾

He says: the earth brings forth what is in its belly of the dead, alive. The dead in the belly of the earth is a burden upon it, and when alive upon its back, it is a burden upon it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from Shabib, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, he said: "The dead."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, he said: "It means the dead."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, "those in the graves."

* *

His saying: ﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And people will say when the earth is shaken for the establishment of the Hour: "What is the matter with the earth, and what is its story?" ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas used to say regarding that:

⁕ Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from Shabib, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾, he said: "The disbeliever says," ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾.

He says: That Day the earth will report its news, and its reporting of its news, according to the statement we mentioned from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, is that it speaks and says: "Indeed God commanded me with this, inspired me to it, and permitted me to do it."

As for Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he used to say regarding that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, he said: I heard Saʿid ibn Jubayr recite in the Maghrib once: ﴿That Day it will report (yunabbi'u) its news﴾, and once: ﴿it will report (tuhaddithu) its news﴾.

So the meaning of tuhaddith, in Saʿid's view, was tunabbi'u (it will inform), and its informing of its news: its bringing forth of its burdens from its belly to its back. This statement is, in my view, sound in meaning, and the interpretation of the speech according to this meaning is: That Day the earth will make clear its news through the quaking and the convulsion, and the bringing forth of the dead from its bellies to its surfaces, by God's inspiration to it and His permission for it. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens, and man says, "What is wrong with it?" That Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it﴾, he said: "He commanded it, so it cast out what was in it and emptied itself."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾, he said: "He commanded it."

It has been mentioned from ʿAbdullah that he used to recite it: ﴿That Day it will inform (tunabbi'u) its news﴾. It was also said: the meaning is that the earth will report its news about those who were upon its back, of the people of obedience and disobedience, and what they did upon it of good or evil.

Those who said so:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾, he said: "what was done upon it of good or evil." ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾, he said: "He informed it of that."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾, he said: "what was in it and upon its back of the deeds of the servants."

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾, he said: "It will inform people of what they did upon it."

It was also said: by His saying: ﴿Because He has inspired it﴾, the meaning is: He inspired to it.

Those who said so:

⁕ Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from Shabib, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Inspired to it﴾, he said: "He inspired to it."

* *

His saying: ﴿That Day the people will depart in scattered groups﴾

It was said: the meaning of this phrase is a delay after ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾. They said: the construction of the speech is: "That Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it, to be shown their deeds; that Day the people will depart in groups." They said: but this phrase intervened between them.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿That Day the people will depart in scattered groups﴾ from the place of reckoning, in divided groups: one taking the right hand to Paradise, and one taking the left hand to the Fire.

* *

His saying: ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾

He says: That Day the people will depart in scattered groups, to the right and to the left, ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾. So the doer of good, who obeyed God in this world, will see his deed and what God has prepared for him that Day of honour in return for his obedience which was in this world; and the evildoer, who disobeyed God, will see his deed and the recompense for his deed and what God has prepared for him of humiliation and disgrace in Hell in return for his disobedience and his disbelief in this world.

* *

His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾

He says: whoever does in this world the weight of an atom of good will see its reward there. ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾: He says: whoever did in this world the weight of an atom of evil will see its recompense there. It was said: "And whoever does" is stated in the future tense while the report concerns the past, for the listeners understand its meaning, owing to the evidence mentioned earlier, that the meaning is "whoever did," as is shown by His saying: ﴿That Day the people will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds﴾. But since the meaning of the speech is understood by the listeners, and since in His saying ﴿does﴾ there is an exhortation to the people of this world to work in obedience to God and a warning against His disobedience, together with the evidence mentioned earlier, that this is intended as a report about a past deed and what is due for it, He brought the report in the form of a report about a future act.

The people of interpretation have said, in accordance with what we have said, that all of them will see their deeds.

Those who said so:

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾, he said: "No believer or disbeliever does good or evil in this world without God giving it to him. As for the believer, he will be shown his good deeds and his evil deeds, and God will forgive him his evil deeds. As for the disbeliever, his good deeds will be returned to him, and he will be punished for his evil deeds." Other than this view has also been stated. Some of them said: "As for the believer, the punishment for his evil deeds is hastened for him in this world, and the reward for his good deeds is deferred; and the disbeliever has the reward for his good deeds hastened for him, and the punishment for his evil deeds deferred."

Those who said so:

⁕ Musa ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi narrated to him, from ʿAmr ibn Qatada, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, while he was explaining this verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight﴾, he said: "Whoever does an atom's weight of good, from a disbeliever, will see its reward in this world in his person, his family, his wealth and his children, until he leaves the world with no good left for him. ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil﴾, from a believer, will see its punishment in this world in his person, his family, his wealth and his children, until he leaves the world with nothing left."

⁕ Mahmud ibn Khidash narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Wasiti narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, he said: I asked Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi about this verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾, he said: "Whoever does an atom's weight of good, from a disbeliever, will see its reward in his person, his family and his wealth, until he leaves the world with no good; and whoever does an atom's weight of evil, from a believer, will see its punishment in his person, his family and his wealth, until he leaves with no evil."

⁕ Abu al-Khattab al-Hassani narrated to me, he said: al-Haytham ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, he said: Sammak ibn ʿAtiyya narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, from Anas, who said: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was eating with the Prophet (ﷺ), when this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. Abu Bakr lifted his hand from the food and said: "O Messenger of God, I am recompensed for what I did of an atom's weight of evil." He said: "O Abu Bakr, what you see in this world of what you dislike is the atoms' weight of evil; and God stores up for you the atoms' weight of good until He pays it to you on the Day of Resurrection."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Ayyub narrated to us, he said: "We found in the book of Abu Qilaba, from Abu Idris, that Abu Bakr was eating with the Prophet (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. Abu Bakr lifted his hand from the food and said: 'Indeed I shall see what I did.'" I do not know except that he said: "what I did of good and evil." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "What you see of what you dislike is the atoms' weight of much evil, and God stores up for you the atoms' weight of good until it is given to you on the Day of Resurrection." And the confirmation of this in the Book of God is: ﴿And whatever misfortune strikes you is for what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, he said: Ayyub narrated to us, he said: I read in the book of Abu Qilaba, he said: The verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ while Abu Bakr was eating with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he paused and said: "O Messenger of God, am I to see what I did of good and evil?" He said: "Have you seen what you have seen of what you dislike? It is from the atoms' weight of evil; and He stores up the atoms' weight of good until you are given it on the Day of Resurrection." Abu Idris said: "I see its confirmation in the Book of God: ﴿And whatever misfortune strikes you is for what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, he said: ʿA'isha said: "O Messenger of God, ʿAbdullah ibn Jud'an used to maintain the ties of kinship, and do such and such; will that benefit him?" He said: "No, for he never once said: 'My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgement.'"

⁕ Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, he said: Hafs narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from ʿA'isha, who said: I said: "O Messenger of God, Ibn Jud'an in the Jahiliyya used to maintain the ties of kinship and feed the poor; will that benefit him?" He said: "It will not benefit him, for he never once said: 'My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgement.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Dawud, from ʿAmir al-Sha'bi, that ʿA'isha, Mother of the Believers, said: "O Messenger of God, ʿAbdullah ibn Jud'an used to maintain the ties of kinship, host the guest, and free captives; will that benefit him at all?" He said: "No, for he never once said: 'My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgement.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Dawud, from ʿAmir, from ʿAlqama, that Salama ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi said: "O Messenger of God, our mother died in the Jahiliyya; she used to maintain the ties of kinship, host the guest, and do such and such; will that benefit her at all?" He said: "No."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: Dawud narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from ʿAlqama ibn Qays, from Salama ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, who said: "My brother and I went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and I said: 'O Messenger of God, our mother in the Jahiliyya used to host the guest and maintain the ties of kinship; will her deed benefit her at all?' He said: 'No.'"

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Sadran and Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, they said: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from ʿAlqama, from Salama ibn Yazid, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in a similar report.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, that he said: "As for the believer, he sees his good deeds in the Hereafter; as for the disbeliever, he sees his good deeds in this world."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: Abu Nuʿama narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Bashir al-Dabbi narrated to us, that his grandfather Salman ibn ʿAmir said: Salman ibn ʿAmir came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "My father used to maintain the ties of kinship, keep covenants, and honour the guest." He said: "Did he die before Islam?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That will not benefit him." So he turned away, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Bring me the old man." He came, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed these deeds will not benefit him, but they will be in his offspring, so you will never be disgraced, you will never be humiliated, and you will never be impoverished."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, he said: ʿImran narrated to us, from Qatada, from Anas, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed God does not wrong the believer in a good deed for which he is rewarded with provision in this world and repaid for in the Hereafter; as for the disbeliever, He gives him for it in this world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will have no good deed."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, he said: Layth narrated to us, he said: al-Mu'alla narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No doer of good, believer or disbeliever, does good except that its reward falls upon God, in the swift of his worldly life or the deferred of his Hereafter."

⁕ Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Yahya ibn ʿAbdullah informed me, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, that he said: "When ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was sitting, and he wept when it was revealed. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: 'What makes you weep, O Abu Bakr?' He said: 'This surah makes me weep.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: 'Were it not that you err and sin, and God forgives you, God would create a nation that errs and sins, and He would forgive them.'"

These reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) indicate that the believer sees the punishment for his evil deeds in this world and the reward for his good deeds in the Hereafter, and that the disbeliever sees the reward for his good deeds in this world and the punishment for his evil deeds in the Hereafter, and that the disbeliever's good deeds from the world will not benefit him in the Hereafter while he remains in disbelief.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿAli narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, he said: "I met seventy of the companions of ʿAbdullah, the youngest of them being al-Harith ibn Suwayd, and I heard him recite: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾ until he reached: ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾, and he said: 'Indeed this is a severe reckoning.'"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 99, verse 1–8 (part 2 of 2):

It was said: the dharrah (tiny particle) is a red worm that has no weight.

Mention of those who said this:

Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Allaf and Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: Shabib ibn Bishr told us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿the weight of an atom's (dharrah) weight﴾. Ibn Sinan said in his narration: "the weight of a red dharrah." And Ibn Wahb said in his narration: "a red ant." Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Harun said: "And they claim that this red worm has no weight."

End of the commentary on Surah Idha Zulzilat al-Ard.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake (1) And the earth brings forth its burdens (2) And man says, "What is wrong with it?" (3) That Day it will report its news (4) Because your Lord has inspired it (5) That Day the people will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds (6) So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it (8)﴾.

His saying, dhikruhu [exalted is He], means: ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ for the establishment of the Hour ﴿with its (final) earthquake﴾, meaning it is violently convulsed. The word zilzal (earthquake) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) when the zay is kasra, and when the zay is fatha it is a noun. The earthquake is attributed to the earth, though it is its attribute, as one says, "I will honour you with your honour," meaning, "I will honour you with honour." This was made good in the phrase zilzaluha because it matches the rhyme endings of the verses that follow.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: "﴿The earth was shaken﴾ in the time of ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud). ʿAbdullah said to it, 'What is the matter with you? Indeed, if it had spoken, the Hour would have been established.'"

His saying, dhikruhu [exalted is He], means: ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ for the establishment of the Hour ﴿with its (final) earthquake﴾, meaning it is violently convulsed. The word zilzal (earthquake) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) when the zay is kasra, and when the zay is fatha it is a noun. The earthquake is attributed to the earth, though it is its attribute, as one says, "I will honour you with your honour," meaning, "I will honour you with honour." This was made good in the phrase zilzaluha because it matches the rhyme endings of the verses that follow.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: "﴿The earth was shaken﴾ in the time of ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud). ʿAbdullah said to it, 'What is the matter with you? Indeed, if it had spoken, the Hour would have been established.'"

* *

His saying: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾

He says: the earth brings forth what is in its belly of the dead, alive. The dead in the belly of the earth is a burden upon it, and when alive upon its back, it is a burden upon it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from Shabib, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, he said: "The dead."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, he said: "It means the dead."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, "those in the graves."

* *

His saying: ﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And people will say when the earth is shaken for the establishment of the Hour: "What is the matter with the earth, and what is its story?" ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas used to say regarding that:

⁕ Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from Shabib, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾, he said: "The disbeliever says," ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾.

He says: That Day the earth will report its news, and its reporting of its news, according to the statement we mentioned from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, is that it speaks and says: "Indeed God commanded me with this, inspired me to it, and permitted me to do it."

As for Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he used to say regarding that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, he said: I heard Saʿid ibn Jubayr recite in the Maghrib once: ﴿That Day it will report (yunabbi'u) its news﴾, and once: ﴿it will report (tuhaddithu) its news﴾.

This statement is, in my view, sound in meaning, and the interpretation of the speech according to this meaning is: That Day the earth will make clear its news through the quaking and the convulsion, and the bringing forth of the dead from its bellies to its surfaces, by God's inspiration to it and His permission for it. It was said: the meaning of this phrase is a delay after ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾. They said: but this phrase intervened between them.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿That Day the people will depart in scattered groups﴾ from the place of reckoning, in divided groups: one taking the right hand to Paradise, and one taking the left hand to the Fire.

* *

His saying: ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾

He says: That Day the people will depart in scattered groups, to the right and to the left, ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾. So the doer of good, who obeyed God in this world, will see his deed and what God has prepared for him that Day of honour in return for his obedience which was in this world; and the evildoer, who disobeyed God, will see his deed and the recompense for his deed and what God has prepared for him of humiliation and disgrace in Hell in return for his disobedience and his disbelief in this world.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 99, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake (1) And the earth brings forth its burdens (2) And man says, "What is wrong with it?" (3) That Day it will report its news (4) Because your Lord has inspired it (5) That Day the people will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds (6) So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it (8)﴾.

His saying, dhikruhu [exalted is He], means: ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ for the establishment of the Hour ﴿with its (final) earthquake﴾, meaning it is violently convulsed. The word zilzal (earthquake) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) when the zay is kasra, and when the zay is fatha it is a noun. The earthquake is attributed to the earth, though it is its attribute, as one says, "I will honour you with your honour," meaning, "I will honour you with honour." This was made good in the phrase zilzaluha because it matches the rhyme endings of the verses that follow.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: "﴿The earth was shaken﴾ in the time of ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud). ʿAbdullah said to it, 'What is the matter with you? Indeed, if it had spoken, the Hour would have been established.'"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 99, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake (1) And the earth brings forth its burdens (2) And man says, "What is wrong with it?" (3) That Day it will report its news (4) Because your Lord has inspired it (5) That Day the people will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds (6) So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it (8)﴾.

His saying, dhikruhu [exalted is He], means: ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ for the establishment of the Hour ﴿with its (final) earthquake﴾, meaning it is violently convulsed. The word zilzal (earthquake) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) when the zay is kasra, and when the zay is fatha it is a noun. The earthquake is attributed to the earth, though it is its attribute, as one says, "I will honour you with your honour," meaning, "I will honour you with honour." This was made good in the phrase zilzaluha because it matches the rhyme endings of the verses that follow.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: "﴿The earth was shaken﴾ in the time of ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud). ʿAbdullah said to it, 'What is the matter with you? Indeed, if it had spoken, the Hour would have been established.'"

* *

His saying: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾

He says: the earth brings forth what is in its belly of the dead, alive. The dead in the belly of the earth is a burden upon it, and when alive upon its back, it is a burden upon it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from Shabib, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, he said: "The dead."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, he said: "It means the dead."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, "those in the graves."

* *

His saying: ﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And people will say when the earth is shaken for the establishment of the Hour: "What is the matter with the earth, and what is its story?" ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas used to say regarding that:

⁕ Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from Shabib, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾, he said: "The disbeliever says," ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾.

He says: That Day the earth will report its news, and its reporting of its news, according to the statement we mentioned from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, is that it speaks and says: "Indeed God commanded me with this, inspired me to it, and permitted me to do it."

As for Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he used to say regarding that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, he said: I heard Saʿid ibn Jubayr recite in the Maghrib once: ﴿That Day it will report (yunabbi'u) its news﴾, and once: ﴿it will report (tuhaddithu) its news﴾.

So the meaning of tuhaddith, in Saʿid's view, was tunabbi'u (it will inform), and its informing of its news: its bringing forth of its burdens from its belly to its back. This statement is, in my view, sound in meaning, and the interpretation of the speech according to this meaning is: That Day the earth will make clear its news through the quaking and the convulsion, and the bringing forth of the dead from its bellies to its surfaces, by God's inspiration to it and His permission for it. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens, and man says, "What is wrong with it?" That Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it﴾, he said: "He commanded it, so it cast out what was in it and emptied itself."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾, he said: "He commanded it."

It has been mentioned from ʿAbdullah that he used to recite it: ﴿That Day it will inform (tunabbi'u) its news﴾. It was also said: the meaning is that the earth will report its news about those who were upon its back, of the people of obedience and disobedience, and what they did upon it of good or evil.

Those who said so:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾, he said: "what was done upon it of good or evil." ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾, he said: "He informed it of that."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾, he said: "what was in it and upon its back of the deeds of the servants."

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿That Day it will report its news﴾, he said: "It will inform people of what they did upon it."

It was also said: by His saying: ﴿Because He has inspired it﴾, the meaning is: He inspired to it.

Those who said so:

⁕ Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from Shabib, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Inspired to it﴾, he said: "He inspired to it."

* *

His saying: ﴿That Day the people will depart in scattered groups﴾

It was said: the meaning of this phrase is a delay after ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾. They said: the construction of the speech is: "That Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it, to be shown their deeds; that Day the people will depart in groups." They said: but this phrase intervened between them.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿That Day the people will depart in scattered groups﴾ from the place of reckoning, in divided groups: one taking the right hand to Paradise, and one taking the left hand to the Fire.

* *

His saying: ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾

He says: That Day the people will depart in scattered groups, to the right and to the left, ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾. So the doer of good, who obeyed God in this world, will see his deed and what God has prepared for him that Day of honour in return for his obedience which was in this world; and the evildoer, who disobeyed God, will see his deed and the recompense for his deed and what God has prepared for him of humiliation and disgrace in Hell in return for his disobedience and his disbelief in this world.

* *

His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾

He says: whoever does in this world the weight of an atom of good will see its reward there. ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾: He says: whoever did in this world the weight of an atom of evil will see its recompense there. It was said: "And whoever does" is stated in the future tense while the report concerns the past, for the listeners understand its meaning, owing to the evidence mentioned earlier, that the meaning is "whoever did," as is shown by His saying: ﴿That Day the people will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds﴾. But since the meaning of the speech is understood by the listeners, and since in His saying ﴿does﴾ there is an exhortation to the people of this world to work in obedience to God and a warning against His disobedience, together with the evidence mentioned earlier, that this is intended as a report about a past deed and what is due for it, He brought the report in the form of a report about a future act.

The people of interpretation have said, in accordance with what we have said, that all of them will see their deeds.

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾, he said: "No believer or disbeliever does good or evil in this world without God giving it to him. As for the believer, he will be shown his good deeds and his evil deeds, and God will forgive him his evil deeds. As for the disbeliever, his good deeds will be returned to him, and he will be punished for his evil deeds." Other than this view has also been stated. Some of them said: "As for the believer, the punishment for his evil deeds is hastened for him in this world, and the reward for his good deeds is deferred; and the disbeliever has the reward for his good deeds hastened for him, and the punishment for his evil deeds deferred."
